top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, KLOwen, Lightforce, self-ligating braces, twin brackets, SmartSTL, Angel, damon ultima brackets
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, rentability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, emergencies decrease, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in bracket systems
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually saves time or money, reduces appointments, or improves practice profitability. Some are skeptical that the workflow changes will translate into real efficiency or financial gains, especially for braces. Others want proof that DM is worth the investment compared to their current recall system.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, only German studies, only Australian studies, only European sources, recent studies, clinical report, clinical cases
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
ROI proof on braces
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes

resources on monitoring braces treatments with damon brackets. Evidence on appointments saved, clinical results, practice optimisation, and oral hygiene benefits. Any evidence on the use of DM with general dental and implant cases would be helpful as well
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for braces and non-Invisalign appliances. Comparative studies with standard recall and breakdowns by practice size/geography are lacking.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, FDA class I, occlusal assessment, accuracy of scanning, AI vs orthodontist, predictability parameters, accuracy in detecting malocclusions
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors express skepticism about whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human orthodontist, especially for clinical observations and diagnostics. Some are concerned about false positives/negatives, regulatory validation, and whether SmartSTL is reliable for treatment planning.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, clinical study, white paper, peer-reviewed, only academic publication, only German studies
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is SmartSTL AI

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct head-to-head studies comparing DM AI/SmartSTL to orthodontist assessments and regulatory validation (FDA/CE) are limited. More peer-reviewed, quantitative accuracy data is needed.

top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are unsure if patients actually prefer DM-monitored treatment, if it improves compliance, or if it adds complexity. Some want to know if DM differentiates their practice or improves staff morale.

top_needs.title: Clinical impact of DM on treatment outcomes, refinements, and case control for aligners
top_needs.brands_and_products: Invisalign, Spark, Angel, clearcorrect, suresmile, SmartSTL
top_needs.metrics_sought: treatment duration, number of refinements, fitting and tracking quality, aligner unseat tracking, compliance, unfinished aligner sets, reduction in refinements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors want proof that DM monitoring reduces the number of refinements, improves aligner tracking, and leads to better or faster outcomes. Some are skeptical that remote monitoring can actually improve clinical results versus standard care.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, retrospective cohort study, only academic publication
sample_queries: Impact on treatment duration
I am looking for fitting and tacking quality between different aligner brands. Specifically Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect and suresmile

Is remote monitoring a reliable method to assess compliance in clear aligner orthodontic treatment?
top_needs.gap_assessment: Comparative studies on refinement rates, treatment duration, and clinical outcomes with and without DM are sparse, especially across multiple aligner brands.
